Vivaldi: Multi-Agent Physiological TS Interpretation (2026)
edges.note: Vivaldi extends single-agent TS reasoning to a multi-agent architecture with specialized clinical roles.

edges.target_label: Vivaldi: Multi-Agent Physiological TS Interpretation (2026)
edges.note: Vivaldi operationalizes biosignal FM concepts via a cooperative multi-agent pipeline for clinical interpretation.

edges.target_label: Vivaldi: Multi-Agent Physiological TS Interpretation (2026)
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text trains a sensor-language bridge, Vivaldi avoids alignment training by distributing interpretation across agents.

edges.target_label: Bridging the Last Mile of Time Series Forecasting with LLM Agents
edges.note: Extends TS-Agent from analysis/reasoning to forecast correction via tool-augmented contextual revision.

edges.source_label: LLMs for Time Series: A Survey (Zhang 2024)
edges.target_label: Bridging the Last Mile of Time Series Forecasting with LLM Agents
edges.note: Fills the deployment gap the survey identified between zero-shot foundation models and usable forecasts.

edges.target_label: Bridging the Last Mile of Time Series Forecasting with LLM Agents
edges.note: The last-mile agent wraps a foundation model forecast (like Sundial) and applies structured revisions using domain context.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: Personalized Deep Learning for Short-Term Forecasting of Impending Atrial Fibrillation from Wearable ECG (2026)
edges.note: Where biosignal foundation models aim for one global model across patients, this paper shows inter-patient ECG variability holds the global model back and per-patient fine-tuning recovers much of the lost accuracy.

edges.target_label: Personalized Deep Learning for Short-Term Forecasting of Impending Atrial Fibrillation from Wearable ECG (2026)
edges.note: Where few-shot health learning adapted a general model to health tasks with small labeled sets, this paper applies the same idea at the level of a single patient's ECG and quantifies how the benefit scales with adaptation data.

edges.target_label: Adaptive Patching Is Harder Than It Looks for Time-Series Forecasting (2026)
edges.note: Where PatchTST fixed a single patch length for long-horizon forecasting, this paper tests content-adaptive patch lengths and shows a validation-tuned uniform size matches them.

edges.target_label: CVAformer: Causal Semantic Alignment for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting (2026)
edges.note: Where Time-LLM aligns raw temporal patterns with frozen language-model embeddings, CVAformer first separates each variable into invariant and dynamic components before alignment.

edges.target_label: CVAformer: Causal Semantic Alignment for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting (2026)
edges.note: Where GPT4TS uses a frozen pretrained transformer as a general time-series backbone, CVAformer keeps that backbone and adds a causal alignment step on top of it.

edges.target_label: CVAformer: Causal Semantic Alignment for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting (2026)
edges.note: Where iTransformer made the channel the unit of tokenization, CVAformer keeps the variable-level view and adds a causal adjustment over it.

edges.target_label: CVAformer: Causal Semantic Alignment for LLM-based Time Series Forecasting (2026)
edges.note: CVAformer imports Pearl-style backdoor adjustment to remove the dynamic component as a confounder during LLM alignment, connecting time series and causal inference.

edges.source_label: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners (MAE, He 2022)
edges.target_label: VAN-AD: Visual Masked Autoencoder with Normalizing Flow for Time Series Anomaly Detection (2026)
edges.note: Where MAE learns image representations by reconstructing masked patches, VAN-AD reuses the masked-reconstruction objective as an anomaly score for multivariate time series.

edges.source_label: How Mask Matters: Masked Autoencoders Theory (Zhang 2023)
edges.target_label: VAN-AD: Visual Masked Autoencoder with Normalizing Flow for Time Series Anomaly Detection (2026)
edges.note: VAN-AD relies on the masked-reconstruction principle this theory work analyzes, then adds a normalizing-flow density model because reconstruction error alone does not give a calibrated probability of abnormality.

edges.source_label: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners (MAE, He 2022)
edges.target_label: HiMAE: Hierarchical Masked Autoencoders Discover Resolution-Specific Structure in Wearable Time Series (2026)
edges.note: Where MAE reconstructs masked image patches with a flat encoder, HiMAE keeps the masked-reconstruction objective but uses a U-Net-style hierarchical convolutional encoder so each level corresponds to a distinct temporal scale of a wearable signal.

edges.source_label: How Mask Matters: Masked Autoencoders Theory (Zhang 2023)
edges.target_label: HiMAE: Hierarchical Masked Autoencoders Discover Resolution-Specific Structure in Wearable Time Series (2026)
edges.note: HiMAE keeps the masked-reconstruction principle this theory work analyzes, then adds a per-level linear probe to measure which temporal resolution carries the predictive signal for a given task.

edges.target_label: HiMAE: Hierarchical Masked Autoencoders Discover Resolution-Specific Structure in Wearable Time Series (2026)
edges.note: Where HARMamba seeks wearable efficiency through a state-space backbone, HiMAE reaches efficiency through convolutional hierarchy and adds a resolution probe that HARMamba lacks.

edges.target_label: HiMAE: Hierarchical Masked Autoencoders Discover Resolution-Specific Structure in Wearable Time Series (2026)
edges.note: HiMAE extends the wearable foundation-model landscape this survey maps, contributing a per-scale analysis rather than added dataset scale.

edges.source_label: VAN-AD: Visual Masked Autoencoder with Normalizing Flow for Time Series Anomaly Detection (2026)
edges.target_label: IMPACT: Influence Modeling for Open-Set Time Series Anomaly Detection (2026)
edges.note: VAN-AD attacks the anomaly score itself as a calibrated likelihood from reconstruction error and density, while IMPACT works one level earlier at the training data, using influence scores to decontaminate labels and to synthesize on-manifold unseen anomalies. Added as a nearest-neighbor link because IMPACT has no direct parent in Leo's library.

edges.source_label: Sensor2Text: NL Interactions for Activity Tracking (Chen 2024)
edges.target_label: PulseLM: A Foundation Dataset and Benchmark for PPG-Text Learning (2026)
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text produced free text from a sensor stream in one activity-tracking setting, PulseLM performs the same waveform-to-language pairing at dataset scale and fixes it into a graded closed-ended benchmark with a shared scoring protocol.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: PulseLM: A Foundation Dataset and Benchmark for PPG-Text Learning (2026)
edges.note: Where the biosignals survey described what a PPG foundation model should look like, PulseLM supplies the standardized data, 1.31 million segments and 3.15 million question-answer pairs, and the evaluation protocol those models need.

edges.target_label: PulseLM: A Foundation Dataset and Benchmark for PPG-Text Learning (2026)
edges.note: PulseLM follows the TS-Agent view of signals as objects queried in language, but turns it into a fixed, reproducible benchmark rather than an agent demonstration.

edges.source_label: How Mask Matters: Masked Autoencoders Theory (Zhang 2023)
edges.target_label: SIGMA-PPG: Statistical-prior Informed Generative Masking Architecture for PPG Foundation Model (2026)
edges.note: Where this theory work shows a high random mask ratio drives masked-autoencoder learning for images, SIGMA-PPG argues random masking is the wrong choice for quasi-periodic signals because the model fills a random gap by copying a neighboring beat, so it learns the mask as a policy and shifts the design knob from how much to mask to where and how hard to mask.

edges.source_label: MAE: Masked Autoencoders Are Scalable Vision Learners (He 2021)
edges.target_label: SIGMA-PPG: Statistical-prior Informed Generative Masking Architecture for PPG Foundation Model (2026)
edges.note: Where MAE established high-ratio random masking for representation learning, SIGMA-PPG replaces the fixed random mask with a reinforcement-learning teacher that builds a curriculum of hard masks from signal statistics such as amplitude and skewness.

edges.source_label: LLMs for Time Series: A Survey (Zhang 2024)
edges.target_label: Time-Series Foundation Model Embeddings for Remaining Useful Life Estimation (2026)
edges.note: Where the survey catalogued ways to attach foundation or language models to time series, this paper takes the plainest version: freeze a pretrained time-series foundation model and train a one-layer regression head, then show the frozen embeddings transfer to remaining-useful-life prediction.

edges.target_label: Time-Series Foundation Model Embeddings for Remaining Useful Life Estimation (2026)
edges.note: Where TS-Agent built a reasoning agent on top of a time-series foundation model, this paper drops the agent and probes the frozen backbone with a light regression head, showing the embeddings alone are competitive with task-specific architectures.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: Time-Series Foundation Model Embeddings for Remaining Useful Life Estimation (2026)
edges.note: Where the biosignal foundation-model survey mapped the design space, this paper supplies a concrete frozen-backbone probing baseline that bio-sensing work can copy before building anything heavier.

edges.target_label: WEQA: Wearable Health Question Answering with Query-Adaptive Agentic Reasoning (2026)
edges.note: Where TS-Agent treated time-series reasoning as an agent calling a fixed set of analysis tools, WEQA adds query-adaptive routing so a sleep question and a cardiac question call different tools.

edges.source_label: Sensor2Text: NL Interactions for Activity Tracking (Chen 2024)
edges.target_label: WEQA: Wearable Health Question Answering with Query-Adaptive Agentic Reasoning (2026)
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text produced a natural-language description of a sensor window, WEQA produces an answer to a specific question, extending the sensor-to-language bridge toward agentic tool routing.

edges.target_label: WEQA: Wearable Health Question Answering with Query-Adaptive Agentic Reasoning (2026)
edges.note: Where Health-LLM showed language models can read health signals from a few examples, WEQA wraps that ability in a controller that plans and routes each wearable-health question to matching tools.

edges.target_label: WEQA: Wearable Health Question Answering with Query-Adaptive Agentic Reasoning (2026)
edges.note: WEQA borrows the plan-and-control idea from LATS but applies the controller to signal-analysis and wearable-model tools rather than to web or code actions.

edges.target_label: HEARTS: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning on Health Time Series
edges.note: HEARTS builds a shared graded benchmark where TS-Agent proposed a single reasoning method, and shows the method-specific wins do not carry over to multi-step reasoning.

edges.target_label: HEARTS: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning on Health Time Series
edges.note: HEARTS tests at scale the few-shot health-learning promise and shows it does not extend to multi-step temporal reasoning.

edges.target_label: HEARTS: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning on Health Time Series
edges.note: HEARTS measures across many modalities and task types rather than the single benchmark ChatTS reported on.

edges.source_label: LLMs for Time Series: A Survey (Zhang 2024)
edges.target_label: HEARTS: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning on Health Time Series
edges.note: HEARTS turns the methods cataloged by the survey into measured baselines on a common test set.

edges.target_label: SLIP: Learning Transferable Sensor Models via Language-Informed Pretraining
edges.note: SLIP removes the fixed-configuration limit of Sensor2Text with a variable-rate patch embedder so one model serves many sensor setups.

edges.target_label: SLIP: Learning Transferable Sensor Models via Language-Informed Pretraining
edges.note: SLIP adds a language target to the self-supervised recipe to capture semantics that reconstruction misses for classification.

edges.target_label: SLIP: Learning Transferable Sensor Models via Language-Informed Pretraining
edges.note: SLIP reuses the frozen language model through cross-attention for alignment and captioning rather than reprogramming it for forecasting.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: FEEL: Quantifying Heterogeneity in Physiological Signals for Generalizable Emotion Recognition
edges.note: FEEL measures the biosignal foundation-model families the survey describes on 19 shared datasets with cross-dataset transfer.

edges.target_label: FEEL: Quantifying Heterogeneity in Physiological Signals for Generalizable Emotion Recognition
edges.note: FEEL evaluates the self-supervised pretraining recipe as one model family and finds handcrafted features stay competitive under noise.

edges.target_label: FEEL: Quantifying Heterogeneity in Physiological Signals for Generalizable Emotion Recognition
edges.note: FEEL benchmarks the signal foundation-model family HeAR represents against classical and deep baselines on EDA and PPG.

edges.target_label: ActivityNarrated: An Open-Ended Narrative Paradigm for Wearable Human Activity Understanding
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text produced fixed descriptions tied to a closed activity vocabulary, ActivityNarrated removes the taxonomy and narrates open-ended behavior over multi-position partially observed streams.

edges.target_label: ActivityNarrated: An Open-Ended Narrative Paradigm for Wearable Human Activity Understanding
edges.note: ActivityNarrated keeps the self-supervised representation idea from SSL for HAR but supervises it by retrieval against free-text narration rather than probing it with a closed classifier.

edges.target_label: SignalMC-MED: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Biosignal Foundation Models on Single-Lead ECG and PPG
edges.note: SignalMC-MED supplies the shared multimodal clinical benchmark the Gu survey called for, fixing paired ECG and PPG tasks so biosignal foundation models can be compared.

edges.target_label: SignalMC-MED: A Multimodal Benchmark for Evaluating Biosignal Foundation Models on Single-Lead ECG and PPG
edges.note: SignalMC-MED evaluates the single-modality biosignal foundation-model family HeAR represents and reports that larger variants do not reliably beat smaller ones.

edges.target_label: Foundation Models Defining A New Era In Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition: A Survey And Outlook
edges.note: The survey places SSL for HAR as a central example of the from-scratch HAR foundation-model direction within its lifecycle taxonomy.

edges.target_label: Foundation Models Defining A New Era In Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition: A Survey And Outlook
edges.note: The survey locates HARMamba among sequence-model encoders adapted to sensor data within its input-to-utilization taxonomy.

edges.target_label: Foundation Models Defining A New Era In Sensor-based Human Activity Recognition: A Survey And Outlook
edges.note: The survey names Sensor2Text as an example of the language-model interaction direction for sensor HAR.

edges.target_label: TimeMaster: Training Time-Series Multimodal LLMs to Reason via Reinforcement Learning (2026)
edges.note: Where DeepSeek-R1 used GRPO to train text-only reasoning, TimeMaster applies the same reward-based recipe to time-series classification and adds a reward term for explanation quality.

edges.source_label: ChatTS: Aligning Time Series with LLMs (Xie 2025)
edges.target_label: TimeMaster: Training Time-Series Multimodal LLMs to Reason via Reinforcement Learning (2026)
edges.note: Where ChatTS aligned a numeric series with language through supervised training, TimeMaster renders the series as an image for a vision-language backbone and shapes the reasoning trace with reinforcement learning.

edges.target_label: TimeMaster: Training Time-Series Multimodal LLMs to Reason via Reinforcement Learning (2026)
edges.note: Where Chain-of-Thought produced reasoning steps by prompting alone, TimeMaster makes those steps a trained, rewarded output format.

edges.source_label: ChatTS: Aligning Time Series with LLMs (Xie 2025)
edges.target_label: TS-Haystack: A Multi-Scale Retrieval Benchmark for Time Series Language Models (2026)
edges.note: Where ChatTS shows an LLM can answer questions about a series, TS-Haystack tests whether it can locate the right part of a long series at all.

edges.target_label: TS-Haystack: A Multi-Scale Retrieval Benchmark for Time Series Language Models (2026)
edges.note: Where TS-Agent reasons over a series with analysis operators, TS-Haystack measures long-context retrieval as an isolated skill.

edges.source_label: LLMs for Time Series: A Survey (Zhang 2024)
edges.target_label: TS-Haystack: A Multi-Scale Retrieval Benchmark for Time Series Language Models (2026)
edges.note: TS-Haystack targets the evaluation gap the survey flagged, namely that existing tests reward short-clip pattern recognition and do not test long-context retrieval.

edges.target_label: When Do Foundation Models Pay Off? A Break-Even Analysis of Pretrained Time Series Forecasters (2026)
edges.note: Where Chronos argued for its own model by reporting aggregate zero-shot wins, this paper measures the task-data size at which a foundation model beats XGBoost.

edges.target_label: When Do Foundation Models Pay Off? A Break-Even Analysis of Pretrained Time Series Forecasters (2026)
edges.note: Where Moirai reported broad zero-shot gains, this paper fixes the deployment decision and asks when the foundation model earns its cost over classical forecasters.

edges.target_label: When Do Foundation Models Pay Off? A Break-Even Analysis of Pretrained Time Series Forecasters (2026)
edges.note: Where PatchTST fixed the supervised architecture, this work fixes the decision procedure and reports the sample size at which the choice flips.

edges.target_label: Forecasting Realized Volatility with Time Series Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where Chronos reported broad zero-shot wins, this paper puts the same model class against HAR econometric baselines on realized volatility and finds the advantage mostly disappears after per-asset averaging.

edges.target_label: Forecasting Realized Volatility with Time Series Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where PatchTST set the neural supervised line, this work tests whether its zero-shot foundation-model descendants beat well-specified econometric benchmarks.

edges.target_label: STELLA: Efficient Sensor-to-LLM Translation for On-Device HAR (2026)
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text produced language from sensors with heavy trainable backbones, STELLA freezes the language model and moves the work into a small hierarchical tokenizer that emits activity-aware tokens, so the system fits on an edge device.

edges.target_label: STELLA: Efficient Sensor-to-LLM Translation for On-Device HAR (2026)
edges.note: Where SSL for HAR pretrained a sensor encoder for later fine-tuning, STELLA does not fine-tune the language model and instead learns only the tokenizer plus a per-user personalization layer, keeping compute and private data on the device.

edges.target_label: STELLA: Efficient Sensor-to-LLM Translation for On-Device HAR (2026)
edges.note: Where LLMs are Few-Shot Health Learners showed a general language model can read physiological signals with few examples, STELLA supplies a learned hierarchical tokenizer that feeds sensor streams to a frozen model on-device.

edges.target_label: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming (2026)
edges.note: Where HARMamba uses a bidirectional recurrent state-space backbone at constant cost per step for activity recognition, TiRex-2 keeps the constant-per-patch recurrent idea but moves to an xLSTM backbone and extends it to multivariate forecasting with future-known covariates and streaming updates.

edges.target_label: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming (2026)
edges.note: Where Bi-Mamba+ applies a bidirectional Mamba to time-series forecasting, TiRex-2 replaces the state-space backbone with an xLSTM backbone and adds an asymmetric grouped-attention variate mixer that mixes across variables while keeping strict causality on the targets.

edges.source_label: LLMs for Time Series: A Survey (Zhang 2024)
edges.target_label: TiRex-2: Generalizing TiRex to Multivariate Data and Streaming (2026)
edges.note: Where the survey frames time-series ability as something to obtain by attaching an LLM, TiRex-2 stays fully numeric and recurrent, sitting on the native-forecasting branch rather than the LLM-integration branch.

edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where DDPM settled the generative-quality question for images and found diffusion the strongest family, SensorGen asks the same question for sensor time series and finds flow-matching, not diffusion, the strongest default, because sensor signals carry measurement noise and time-frequency structure that images do not.

edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where Diffusion Beats GANs showed diffusion overtakes GANs on image fidelity, SensorGen re-runs that comparison for sensor signals under a single 14-setting protocol and finds the ranking does not transfer.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where Gu 2025 surveyed biosignal models and named the lack of systematic comparison as a gap, SensorGen fills it with a controlled study across 4 domains, 7 datasets, and 12 signal modalities.

edges.target_label: Signal or Noise? Understanding Generative Models for Real-World Sensor Time Series (SensorGen, 2026)
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text modeled sensor signals toward downstream use, SensorGen measures whether generated sensor signals improve downstream prediction, not only visual realism.

edges.target_label: Post-Training in Time Series Foundation Models: A Unifying Framework (2026)
edges.note: Where Chronos supplied a single pretrained time series model, this survey treats that model as the starting state and maps the methods that adapt it after pretraining into five families.

edges.target_label: Post-Training in Time Series Foundation Models: A Unifying Framework (2026)
edges.note: Where TS-Agent added statistical context around a series through a language-model controller, this survey names that move context augmentation and places it against the other four post-training families.

edges.target_label: Post-Training in Time Series Foundation Models: A Unifying Framework (2026)
edges.note: Where Time-LLM reprogrammed a language model backbone for forecasting, this survey names that move model composition and separates it from context augmentation on a shared map keyed by locus of intervention.

edges.target_label: Expert-Guided Forecast Editing for Time-Series Foundation Models (DEFT, 2026)
edges.note: Where Chronos produces a fixed forecast, DEFT keeps the model frozen and edits that forecast at test time, reusing its predictive samples inside a trend-seasonal decomposition.

edges.target_label: Expert-Guided Forecast Editing for Time-Series Foundation Models (DEFT, 2026)
edges.note: Where the sample-efficient cross-entropy method searches the horizon as one unstructured high-dimensional vector, DEFT explores component-wise and reuses each expert score across trend and seasonal components so a scarce query buys more information.

edges.source_label: Post-Training in Time Series Foundation Models: A Unifying Framework (2026)
edges.target_label: Expert-Guided Forecast Editing for Time-Series Foundation Models (DEFT, 2026)
edges.note: Where the post-training survey named calibrated output processing with test-time guidance as an open direction, DEFT supplies a concrete method for it.

edges.target_label: Zero-Shot HRV Forecasting from Consumer Wearables Using Time Series Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where Chronos established a general zero-shot time-series forecaster on clean broad benchmarks, this paper runs it unchanged on artifact-rich wearable HRV and shows it still beats classical baselines.

edges.target_label: Zero-Shot HRV Forecasting from Consumer Wearables Using Time Series Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: MOIRAI is one of the three pretrained universal forecasters tested here, moved from broad benchmarks to fragmented consumer-wearable HRV with no fine-tuning.

edges.target_label: Zero-Shot HRV Forecasting from Consumer Wearables Using Time Series Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where TS-Agent treats time series as a reasoning problem for a language model, this paper stays with pure forecasting and asks only whether the pretrained forecaster generalizes to a new signal type.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: Zero-Shot HRV Forecasting from Consumer Wearables Using Time Series Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where the biosignals survey catalogs transfer of foundation models to physiological signals, this paper supplies a concrete zero-shot baseline on wearable HRV and isolates data fragmentation, not model capacity, as the engineering problem.

edges.target_label: OpenMHC: Accelerating the Science of Wearable Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where GLOBEM released a multi-year, multi-site wearable behavior dataset with a cross-dataset benchmark, OpenMHC releases a larger open dataset together with open model weights and a three-track benchmark, moving the blocking problem from whether pretraining works to reproducibility and fair comparison.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: OpenMHC: Accelerating the Science of Wearable Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where the biosignals survey mapped the design space and pretraining strategies for biosignal foundation models, OpenMHC supplies the shared dataset, reference implementations, and benchmark needed to compare those strategies in one place.

edges.source_label: Self-supervised Learning for HAR with 700K Person-days (Yuan 2024)
edges.target_label: OpenMHC: Accelerating the Science of Wearable Foundation Models (2026)
edges.note: Where Yuan 2024 showed large-scale self-supervised pretraining works on a single accelerometer stream, OpenMHC broadens the input to 19 sensor channels and links them to health and mood outcomes inside one standardized benchmark.

edges.source_label: Foundation Models for Biosignals: A Survey (Gu 2025)
edges.target_label: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models (BLPM) (2026)
edges.note: Where the survey observed that masked reconstruction leaves biosignal encoders optimising signal fidelity rather than clinical semantics, BLPM changes the objective itself and predicts a latent target instead of the trace.

edges.source_label: Sensor2Text: NL Interactions for Activity Tracking (Chen 2024)
edges.target_label: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models (BLPM) (2026)
edges.note: Where Sensor2Text bridged an already-trained sensor encoder to language afterwards, BLPM makes semantic alignment part of the representation through multi-query decomposition, because a projection head cannot recover what the pretraining objective discarded.

edges.source_label: How Mask Matters: Masked Autoencoders Theory (Zhang 2023)
edges.target_label: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models (BLPM) (2026)
edges.note: Where Zhang 2023 explained that masked reconstruction learns whatever structure the mask forces it to learn, BLPM treats that as a diagnosis of the objective rather than of its hyperparameters and removes the reconstruction target.

edges.target_label: Continuous-Latent Predictive Modeling with Semantic Alignment for EEG-Language Foundation Models (BLPM) (2026)
edges.note: SensorLM scaled sensor-language pretraining on wearable streams; BLPM carries the same alignment idea into neural signals and replaces one pooled embedding with several task-decomposed queries.

edges.target_label: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement (2026)
edges.note: Where TimeGrad fits a probabilistic generative model to the whole series distribution and is therefore dominated by the bulk, TailBooster leaves the generator weak on purpose and conditions the training set on the tail instead.

edges.target_label: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement (2026)
edges.note: GAN-family tabular synthesis is the conventional baseline TailBooster measures against; the change is not a better generator but a restricted training subset plus a rejection step.

edges.target_label: TailBooster: A Dual-Layer Generative Framework for Extreme Value Augmentation with Operational Validity Enforcement (2026)
edges.note: Where l-DAE used autoencoder denoising to improve what a generator produces, TailBooster inverts the same machinery and uses reconstruction error as a rejection criterion over samples already produced.
